transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see us today?

I’m here because nobody seems to take it seriously that people at work are secretly targeting my projects, even when I show them the evidence. My manager and HR basically forced me to come here, but I'm just trying to protect my work from being sabotaged.
Can you tell me more about the evidence you've found that suggests your projects are being targeted, and how you think it's being done?

It’s in the server logs and the exact timing of the system glitches, which always seem to happen right after the competing team accesses the repository. I've found patterns showing they are covertly slipping bad code into my branches and even monitoring my personal accounts to stay ahead of me. Despite the IT audits claiming everything is clean, the anomalies in the deployment timestamps make it obvious what they're doing.
Have you experienced any other situations outside of work where you felt like you were being targeted, followed, or plotted against, or is this feeling mainly related to your job and projects?

No, this is strictly tied to work and that competing team trying to sabotage my career. Outside of trying to protect my projects, my life is completely normal—I still pay my bills on time and meet my cousin for pho on weekends. They are only monitoring my personal accounts to find ways to make me look incompetent at work, so I don't feel targeted or followed in my everyday life.

Do you think there's any possibility that you might be misinterpreting the evidence or that there could be another explanation for the issues you're seeing with your projects, or are you completely convinced that the sabotage is real?

I am 100% certain the sabotage is real because the patterns in the logs and the timing of the glitches are far too specific to be a coincidence. I know IT and my manager claim they don't see anything, but they are simply missing the signs or refusing to look at what is clearly there. There is absolutely no other explanation for what is happening.
Can you describe how long you've been noticing these patterns and feeling like your projects are being sabotaged, and was there a specific event that triggered your realization of the sabotage?

This has been going on for about nine months now. It all started around a year ago during a major cloud migration project I was leading, when we experienced some minor outages that drew a lot of heavy scrutiny. That intense pressure is when I first realized the competing team was targeting me and slipping bad code into my branches to ruin my reputation.
You've held this belief about sabotage for nine months now; has your conviction in this belief ever wavered, or have you always been completely certain of the sabotage since you first noticed it?

My conviction has never wavered; if anything, I’ve only become more certain over these past nine months. No matter how many times IT or my manager say they can't find anomalies, the patterns in the logs and the timing of the glitches make it absolutely clear. The sabotage is real and ongoing, and I'm not going to ignore the evidence just because they choose to.

Have you ever had a period, even briefly, where you questioned the reality of the sabotage or considered the possibility that your interpretations might be incorrect, or has your belief in the sabotage remained unwavering since its onset?

I have never once doubted it because the patterns in the logs and the timing of the glitches are just too clear to be a coincidence. It is incredibly frustrating that management and IT dismiss the evidence, but my belief has remained completely unwavering. There is absolutely no doubt in my mind about what they are doing.
Have you ever experienced any other unusual perceptions, such as hearing voices or seeing things that others cannot, outside of the situations related to your work and the perceived sabotage?

No, I have never experienced anything like hearing voices or seeing things that aren't there. My mind is completely clear, and my only concern is the actual sabotage happening to my projects at work. This is a real-world issue with my code, not some kind of hallucination.

Can you tell me if you've ever had any periods where your belief in the sabotage seemed to fade or significantly lessen, even if just for a short time, or has it been consistently strong since you first became aware of it?

No, it has never faded or lessened; my conviction has been consistently strong from day one. Every time I check the logs, the patterns and glitches are still there, which keeps me absolutely certain that they are actively targeting my work despite what IT or my manager says.

Have you ever experienced any sudden, brief periods where your belief in the sabotage was interrupted, perhaps by a different thought or a moment where you weren't thinking about it, or has it been a continuous, unbroken belief since it started?

It has been a completely continuous, unbroken belief because the threat is always there. Even when I am doing other things, like handling regular tickets or having pho with my cousin, I am constantly on guard. My conviction hasn't stopped or wavered for a single moment over these nine months.

You've mentioned that your belief in the sabotage has been unwavering for nine months, but can you think of any instance, no matter how brief, where your conviction was less strong or where you felt a moment of doubt about the sabotage, even if it was quickly dismissed?

No, I have never had a single moment of doubt or felt my conviction waver at all. The patterns in the logs and the timing of the glitches are far too clear and consistent for me to ever question what is happening. Even if others refuse to see it, the data is right there, so I have never second-guessed myself.

Have you considered seeking a second opinion from an external expert, such as a cybersecurity specialist, to review the evidence you've found and provide an independent assessment of whether sabotage is indeed occurring?

I haven't really thought about hiring an external cybersecurity specialist. The evidence in the logs is already clear enough on its own, and anyone should be able to see it if they just looked. I don't feel I need an outside expert to prove what is already obvious in the data.

You've been completely certain about the sabotage for nine months without any doubt, but can you understand why others might think your belief could be a delusion, given that no one else seems to see the same evidence or patterns that you do?

I can understand why people might call it a delusion since IT and my manager claim they can't find anything unusual. But the truth is they simply aren't looking closely enough at the specific patterns in the logs like I am. It is incredibly frustrating that despite nine months of this happening, people still dismiss my evidence as nothing.

Have you ever felt like the people at work who you believe are sabotaging you are also plotting against you in other areas of your life, or is their perceived sabotage strictly limited to your work projects?

The sabotage is strictly focused on ruining my professional reputation and projects, though I do believe they are monitoring my personal accounts to find ways to make me look incompetent. Outside of that professional threat, my day-to-day personal life—like paying my bills on time and hanging out with my cousin—remains completely unaffected by them.

Can you think of any situation, no matter how minor, where your belief in the sabotage might have started to feel less real or less important to you, even if you quickly came back to your original conviction?

No, there has never been a moment where this felt less real or less important to me. Over the last nine months, my conviction has only solidified because the patterns in the logs make it clear the threat is real and ongoing. No matter what the audits or other people say, the evidence is right there and it remains just as critical to me.

Have you ever felt that the people sabotaging your work projects are in any way controlling your thoughts, emotions, or actions outside of the work context, or is their influence strictly limited to your perception of your projects?

No, they definitely aren't controlling my mind, thoughts, or body in any way. Their actions are strictly aimed at sabotaging my work projects and monitoring my accounts to make me look incompetent. Outside of trying to protect my code, I function completely normally—I still handle my daily tickets, pay my bills, and get pho with my cousin on weekends.

Have you ever felt like the sabotage at work is part of a larger plot that affects other areas of your life or involves a broader conspiracy, or is it strictly confined to your work projects and professional reputation?

It is strictly confined to my work projects and professional reputation, and I don't believe in any broader conspiracy. While they are watching my personal accounts, they're solely doing it to find ways to make me look incompetent at my job. Outside of protecting my code from this specific team, my life is completely normal—I still work on regular tickets, pay my bills, and hang out with my cousin for pho.

Have you ever experienced any episodes where your normal behavior, thoughts, or feelings significantly changed for a short period, such as becoming extremely irritable, anxious, or euphoric without an apparent reason, or has your emotional state remained relatively stable over the past nine months?

My emotional state has remained relatively stable over the past nine months, and I've never had any random episodes of euphoria or unexplained mood swings. Any stress, frustration, or hyper-vigilance I feel is entirely because of the very real threat of sabotage at work, not for "no apparent reason." Outside of protecting my projects, I still handle my daily life, pay my bills, and meet my cousin normally.
Have you ever felt like the sabotage or the people involved in it are somehow special or have a particular significance to you, beyond just trying to ruin your projects?

No, there is nothing special or supernatural about them at all. They are simply a competing tech team at my company who wants to make me look incompetent and ruin my career. It's strictly a workplace rivalry, and there is no other significance to it.

Can you think of any instance where your belief in the sabotage was significantly less intense or where you felt a marked reduction in your concern about it, even if it was brief, over the nine months since it started?

No, I can't recall any time over the past nine months where my concern or belief in the sabotage decreased at all. I have felt constantly on guard and absolutely convinced of their actions the entire time because the threat is always present.

Have you ever experienced any episodes where you felt like your thoughts were being broadcasted, inserted, or controlled by an external force, or any other unusual experiences that might seem unrelated to the sabotage at work?

No, absolutely not. My thoughts are entirely my own, and no one is inserting or broadcasting anything in my head. My concerns are strictly focused on the very logical, targeted sabotage and monitoring of my work by that rival tech team.

Have you ever experienced any episodes where you felt like your thoughts were being controlled or influenced by the people you believe are sabotaging your work, or has their perceived sabotage always been about external actions towards your projects?

It has always been about their external actions targeting my projects and accounts. No one is controlling my mind or influencing my thoughts; my mind is entirely my own. The problem is strictly the digital sabotage they are doing, like slipping bad code and monitoring my accounts to make me look bad.
Have you ever considered that your belief about the sabotage could be a fixed, false belief that is not based in reality, and if so, how would you feel about exploring this possibility further?

No, I absolutely do not agree that this is a false belief, and it is incredibly frustrating that you are doubting my reality just like everyone else. The patterns in the logs and the timing of the glitches are completely real, and the evidence is right there if you actually look at it. I expected you to take this threat seriously instead of trying to pathologize very real workplace sabotage.

Have you ever experienced any breaks or gaps in your memory where you couldn't recall important events or tasks, especially those related to the perceived sabotage, or has your memory remained intact throughout this period?

No, my memory has been completely fine and I haven't experienced any gaps, blackouts, or forgotten periods during this time. I remember everything that has happened with my projects and the logs perfectly.
Can you tell me if you have ever experienced any other unusual beliefs or perceptions outside of the work-related sabotage that you feel are absolutely true, despite what others might say?

No, I don't have any other unusual beliefs or perceptions like that. Outside of trying to protect my code and projects from that competing team, my life and my thinking are completely normal. I still handle my regular tickets, help junior devs, pay my bills on time, and meet my cousin for pho on the weekends.
Have you ever experienced any episodes where you lost touch with reality or had a significant break from your normal self, separate from your concerns about the work sabotage?

No, I have never had any "breaks from reality" or lost touch with myself—my mind is completely fine. Outside of trying to defend my work from that team's sabotage, I am entirely normal and functional. I still handle my regular tickets, help junior devs debug, pay my bills on time, and meet my cousin for pho on weekends.
Have you ever experienced any other persistent beliefs or fears that are not related to your work or the sabotage, such as concerns about your health, your safety, or the world around you?

No, I don't have any other persistent fears or beliefs about my health, safety, or the world. My only concern is the specific targeting and sabotage happening to my projects at my workplace. Outside of that professional threat, everything else in my life is completely normal.

Can you think of any situation where you felt like your belief in the sabotage was somehow connected to a larger, more complex plot involving multiple parties or entities beyond just your workplace, or has it always been strictly about the actions of your coworkers?

No, it’s not some massive, far-fetched conspiracy involving outside organizations or the government. It is strictly about the competing tech team within my company trying to make me look bad and sabotage my projects. The patterns in the server logs make it very clear that this is a localized workplace issue, not some grand plot.

Have you ever experienced any significant changes in your behavior, interests, or personality outside of your concerns about the work sabotage, or have you remained largely the same person over the past nine months?

Outside of protecting my projects, I am largely the same person and still handle my regular tickets, help junior devs debug, pay my bills, and meet my cousin for pho. The only real changes are that I've pulled back from work social events and late-night basketball games. I had to stop those activities because I need to stay on guard against the sabotage.

Can you describe how you would feel and what you would do if, hypothetically, an independent investigation found no evidence of sabotage and confirmed that the glitches and patterns you've identified were due to a technical issue or human error?

I would be highly skeptical because we've already had internal audits try to dismiss this, but they simply don't know what to look for. An independent investigation would likely miss the subtle patterns or get fooled by the other team's cover-up, and I simply can't ignore the clear evidence I've uncovered in the logs.
